#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""One reader for unit readouts: the status strip, the session-start note and
a person all read the same files.

A readout is one JSON file directly in `.agents/.readout/`:

    {"strip": "<short line or empty>", "note": "<text or empty>",
     "written_at": "<ISO-8601 UTC>", "session": "<session id>",
     "stale_after": <seconds>}

`session` is absent for a repository-wide readout, which is stored as
`<name>.json`; a session-scoped one is `<name>--<session>.json`, so two
sessions never overwrite each other. A name is lower-case words joined by
single hyphens. A session id keeps only [A-Za-z0-9_-], on write and on read.
`stale_after` (seconds, default 86400) is how long the readout is current;
past it, its strip segment and note carry its age: `(12m old)`, `(30h old)`,
`(3d old)`.

Only `*.json` files are readouts; any other file in the folder is the
writing unit's own ledger. Lifetime: `prune` (run at session start) removes
session-scoped readouts written over 7 days ago, `.write-*.tmp` files over an
hour old, and any other file whose mtime is over 7 days old, except a `*.lock`
file, so a unit that keeps a ledger here must touch it at least weekly. Repository-wide
readouts are never pruned; their writer owns them.

Strip text has every control character turned into a space. A note keeps its
newlines, turns other control characters into spaces, and is cut at 12 lines.

A readout is visible to a session when it carries no `session` or the same
one. A file that does not parse, or has no usable `written_at`, is reported as
`<name>: unreadable` rather than skipped, and never makes the reader fail:
the exit status is non-zero only for bad arguments.

Usage:
  readout.py write <name> [--session ID] [--strip TEXT] [--note TEXT]
                      [--stale-after SECONDS] [--repo DIR]
  readout.py strip <repo> <session>
  readout.py note  <repo> <session>
  readout.py show  [--repo DIR] [--session ID] [--all]
  readout.py prune <repo>
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import tempfile
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

NAME = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*")
SESSION_DROP = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]")
CONTROL = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x1f\x7f-\x9f]")
CONTROL_KEEPING_NEWLINE = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x09\x0b-\x1f\x7f-\x9f]")
SEGMENT_MAX = 60
NOTE_MAX_LINES = 12
DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER = 86400
PRUNE_SESSION_AFTER = timedelta(days=7)
PRUNE_FILE_AFTER = timedelta(days=7)
PRUNE_TEMP_AFTER = timedelta(hours=1)
SEPARATOR = "  ·  "
# Readouts that lead the strip: the host cuts the row at the terminal width,
# so what must stay visible comes first. Others follow in file-name order.
STRIP_FIRST = ("owed",)
DEFAULT_REPO = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3])


def folder(repo):
    return Path(repo) / ".agents" / ".readout"


def clean_session(session):
    """The one session-id form, used on write and on read."""
    return SESSION_DROP.sub("", session or "")


def write(repo, name, *, strip="", note="", session=None, stale_after=DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER):
    """Write one readout atomically and return its path."""
    if not NAME.fullmatch(name):
        raise ValueError(f"readout name {name!r} must be lower-case words joined by single hyphens")
    if stale_after < 0:
        raise ValueError("stale_after must be zero or more seconds")
    record = {
        "strip": strip,
        "note": note,
        "written_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
        "stale_after": stale_after,
    }
    if session:
        session = clean_session(session)
        if not session:
            raise ValueError("session id has no [A-Za-z0-9_-] character")
        record["session"] = session
    directory = folder(repo)
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target = directory / (f"{name}--{record['session']}.json" if session else f"{name}.json")
    handle, temp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".write-", suffix=".tmp")
    try:
        with os.fdopen(handle, "w", encoding="utf-8") as out:
            json.dump(record, out)
            out.write("\n")
        os.replace(temp, target)
    except BaseException:
        Path(temp).unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise
    return target


class Readout:
    def __init__(self, path):
        self.path = path
        self.name = CONTROL.sub(" ", path.stem)
        self.stale_after = DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER
        self.strip = ""
        self.note = ""
        self.session = None
        self.written_at = None
        self.readable = False
        try:
            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.written_at = datetime.fromisoformat(str(data["written_at"]).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
            if self.written_at.tzinfo is None:
                self.written_at = self.written_at.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
            self.strip = str(data.get("strip") or "")
            self.note = str(data.get("note") or "")
            self.session = clean_session(str(data.get("session") or ""))
            self.stale_after = int(data.get("stale_after", DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER))
            self.readable = True
        except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError):
            return
        suffix = f"--{self.session}"
        if self.session and self.name.endswith(suffix):
            self.name = self.name[: -len(suffix)]

    def visible_to(self, session):
        return not self.readable or not self.session or self.session == clean_session(session)

    def age(self, now):
        """` (12m old)`, ` (30h old)` or ` (3d old)` past stale_after, else nothing."""
        elapsed = (now - self.written_at).total_seconds()
        if elapsed <= self.stale_after:
            return ""
        minutes = int(elapsed // 60)
        if minutes < 60:
            return f" ({minutes}m old)"
        hours = minutes // 60
        return f" ({hours}h old)" if hours < 48 else f" ({hours // 24}d old)"


def readouts(repo):
    directory = folder(repo)
    if not directory.is_dir():
        return []
    return [Readout(path) for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.json")) if path.is_file()]


def visible(repo, session, include_all=False):
    return [r for r in readouts(repo) if include_all or r.visible_to(session)]


def cut(text):
    text = CONTROL.sub(" ", text)
    return text if len(text) <= SEGMENT_MAX else text[: SEGMENT_MAX - 1] + "…"


def show_command(session):
    """The command, runnable from the repository root, that shows what a
    session may see; without a session, every readout."""
    session = clean_session(session)
    flag = f"--session {session}" if session else "--all"
    return f"python3 .agents/hooks/lib/readout.py show {flag}"


def note_lines(note, limit, command):
    """The note with control characters (newlines kept) turned into spaces,
    cut to `limit` lines, with `command` named, when a limit is given."""
    lines = CONTROL_KEEPING_NEWLINE.sub(" ", note).split("\n")
    if limit is not None and len(lines) > limit:
        hidden = len(lines) - limit
        lines = lines[:limit] + [f"… {hidden} more lines: {command}"]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def death_segments(repo):
    """`<run>/<lane> died <cause>` or `<run>/<cell> parked` for each active lane whose claimant,
    and each cell out whose agent, the death reader's cache judges dead or parked; a cell sent
    out again ignores its earlier agent's death. The cache is read as it stands: the strip runs
    at every refresh and never runs the reader. A missing cache shows nothing; one that cannot
    be read shows `deaths: unreadable`."""
    state = Path(repo) / ".agents" / ".workloop-state.json"
    try:
        data = json.loads(state.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return []
    # Not at the top: write and show run from a copy of this file alone.
    import agent_deaths
    import agent_silence
    import agent_verdicts
    try:
        dead = agent_deaths.judged_dead(Path(repo))
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError):
        return ["deaths: unreadable"]
    segments = []
    for run_name, run in (data.get("runs") or {}).items():
        if run.get("torn_down"):
            continue
        held = [(name, lane.get("claimed_by"), None) for name, lane in (run.get("lanes") or {}).items()
                if lane.get("state") == "active"]
        held += [(name, cell.get("agent_id"), agent_silence.parse(cell.get("out_since")))
                 for name, cell in (run.get("cells") or {}).items() if cell.get("state") == "out"]
        for name, agent, since in held:
            if verdict := agent_verdicts.dead_since(dead, agent, since):
                segments.append(cut(f"{run_name}/{name} " + ("parked" if verdict.state == "parked" else f"died {verdict.cause}")))
    return segments


def strip_line(repo, session):
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    segments = []
    # sorted is stable, so file-name order holds within each group.
    for readout in sorted(visible(repo, session), key=lambda r: r.name not in STRIP_FIRST):
        if not readout.readable:
            segments.append(f"{readout.name}: unreadable")
        elif readout.strip:
            segments.append(cut(readout.strip) + readout.age(now))
    return SEPARATOR.join(segments + death_segments(repo))


def note_text(repo, session):
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    lines = []
    for readout in visible(repo, session):
        if not readout.readable:
            lines.append(f"{readout.name}: unreadable")
        elif readout.note:
            lines.append(f"{readout.name}{readout.age(now)}: {note_lines(readout.note, NOTE_MAX_LINES, show_command(session))}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def show_text(repo, session, include_all):
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    blocks = []
    for readout in visible(repo, session, include_all):
        if not readout.readable:
            blocks.append(f"{readout.name}: unreadable ({readout.path.name})")
            continue
        scope = f" [session {readout.session}]" if readout.session else ""
        age = readout.age(now) or f" (written {readout.written_at.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')}Z)"
        block = [f"{readout.name}{scope}{age}"]
        if readout.strip:
            block.append(f"  strip: {CONTROL.sub(' ', readout.strip)}")
        if readout.note:
            block.append("  note: " + note_lines(readout.note, None, None).replace("\n", "\n    "))
        blocks.append("\n".join(block))
    return "\n".join(blocks)


def prune(repo):
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    for readout in readouts(repo):
        if readout.readable and readout.session and now - readout.written_at > PRUNE_SESSION_AFTER:
            readout.path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    directory = folder(repo)
    if not directory.is_dir():
        return
    for path in directory.iterdir():
        # A lock file's mtime never moves while it is in use, and a unit's writers lock on it.
        if not path.is_file() or path.suffix in (".json", ".lock"):
            continue
        limit = PRUNE_TEMP_AFTER if path.name.startswith(".write-") and path.suffix == ".tmp" else PRUNE_FILE_AFTER
        if now - datetime.fromtimestamp(path.stat().st_mtime, timezone.utc) > limit:
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def main(argv):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="readout.py", description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    w = sub.add_parser("write")
    w.add_argument("name")
    w.add_argument("--session")
    w.add_argument("--strip", default="")
    w.add_argument("--note", default="")
    w.add_argument("--stale-after", type=int, default=DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER, metavar="SECONDS")
    w.add_argument("--repo", default=DEFAULT_REPO)

    for name in ("strip", "note"):
        p = sub.add_parser(name)
        p.add_argument("repo")
        p.add_argument("session")

    s = sub.add_parser("show")
    s.add_argument("--repo", default=DEFAULT_REPO)
    s.add_argument("--session", default="")
    s.add_argument("--all", action="store_true")

    p = sub.add_parser("prune")
    p.add_argument("repo")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.command == "write":
        try:
            write(args.repo, args.name, strip=args.strip, note=args.note, session=args.session,
                  stale_after=args.stale_after)
        except ValueError as error:
            parser.error(str(error))
    elif args.command == "strip":
        line = strip_line(args.repo, args.session)
        if line:
            print(line)
    elif args.command == "note":
        text = note_text(args.repo, args.session)
        if text:
            print(text)
    elif args.command == "show":
        text = show_text(args.repo, args.session, args.all)
        if text:
            print(text)
    else:
        prune(args.repo)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

.agents/eval/review-harness/README.md
# Review harness

Run the shipped hostile-review contract against real code with the whole
repository present. Check that it flags conformance and finds real defects.

## Why this exists

`fixtures/review-episodes/` holds 41 adjudicated findings, but each fixture
gives the reviewer a diff only. The reference findings were written with full
repository access over several rounds. A reviewer with a diff cannot reach what
the reference author reached, so recall floors and the corpus cannot rank
anything.

This harness reconstructs the repository as the original reviewer saw it. The
difference is large. Reviewers here cite files three hops outside the diff.

## What it measures

The contract makes one line mandatory: a conformance statement before the
findings. `bin/score.py` reports whether each run produced it. That column is
the reason the harness runs.

Recall against the reference is reported too, as a descriptive column only.

CAUTION: Recall measures agreement with one earlier reviewer. It cannot
separate "found fewer defects" from "found different defects". Treat a low
number as a question, never as a verdict.

## Results so far

Eight runs across two fixtures, sonnet, one constant genome. Their reports are
`results/phase0/`, keyed by `results/phase0/blind-key.tsv`.

`runs.tsv` is the ledger `bin/run-review.sh` appends to, and it starts after
phase 0 — the eight runs above are not in it and cannot be backfilled honestly,
because no record holds the contract hash and base commit each one ran against.
Its two rows are runs that were materialised and never graded, which is what
`pending` says. Read `runs.tsv` for what the harness has measured since phase 0,
and this section for phase 0 itself.

- 4 of 8 runs opened with a conformance statement. A fifth stated one after a
  paragraph of process narration, which the mandatory line now rules out. Three
  of the four misses were on `saas-audit-web-disconnect-r1`. Re-measure after
  the next batch.

  NOTE: `score.py` detects the conformance line by keyword. That is crude and
  it disagrees with a careful read at the margin. Hand-check the column while
  the sample is this small.
- Recall was 1 of 12 on the best-documented fixture, below the diff-only
  baseline of 3.00. The unmatched findings were real. One run found that
  `clear_and_delete_domains` swallows `SoftTimeLimitExceeded` in a broad
  `except`, where `backend/database.py:114` and
  `backend/workers/dns_health_worker.py:1049` re-raise it on purpose.
- All four `saas-audit-web-disconnect-r1` runs found that `.btn--danger` is
  undefined, so the destructive confirm button renders as the primary action.
  That defect is absent from the 8-entry reference.

Raw reports are in `results/phase0/`.

CAUTION: Phase 0 and the two `pending` rows ran before the contract defined a
severity floor and `FINDINGS: none`. `runs.tsv` keys each run to a
`contract_sha`, and that value changed. Findings per run is therefore not
comparable across the change. Re-measure both fixtures under the current
contract before you read any movement as an effect.

## Run one review

```sh
bin/extract-contract.sh                          # sync contract.md with the shipped file
bin/run-review.sh <fixture> <replicate>          # materialise, print the prompt
# dispatch a subagent with that prompt; save its returned text to report.md
bin/build-reference.py ../../fixtures/review-episodes/<fixture>/ground-truth.md ref/<fixture>.md
bin/prepare-grading.py <fixture>                 # anonymise into a grading dir
# dispatch a grader with TASK.md; save its tables to grades.tsv
bin/score.py <fixture>
```

Scenario trees live under `$REVIEW_HARNESS_WORK`, default `$TMPDIR/rvw`. They
are not committed.

## Human evaluation

Automated scoring measures a proxy. The operator is the ground truth: they act
on the findings. So the primary evaluation is a blind human pick.

Present the reviews of one change side by side, labels shuffled, contract
identity held in `results/*/blind-key.tsv`. The operator picks the review they
would rather receive and states one line on why.

Record every verdict in `judgements.tsv` as `set, pick, criterion, note`. The
`criterion` column is the valuable one. "B is better" teaches nothing; "named
the failing constraint instead of a canned string" is a rule that transfers.

CAUTION: Do not rely on mining session transcripts for these verdicts later.
Write the row when the judgement is made. Accumulated rows become the
calibration set for a preference judge, which is a different and more tractable
thing than a correctness oracle.

Keep batches small. Each report runs 1000 to 1500 words, so three of them is
real attention. Four sets that agree carry more weight than twelve rushed ones.

## Materialisation

DANGER: Never extract the tree at `commit_sha`. Four of the five artifacts are
working-tree snapshots taken at the moment of review dispatch. The commit that
followed folded the review fixes in. Its tree holds repaired code for the exact
defects the reviewer must find.

`run-review.sh` extracts at `base_sha` and applies the artifact. All three
`diff` artifacts apply clean. Both `file` artifacts have a target path that
exists at the base.

`fixtures-extra/` holds files an artifact carries as raw text instead of diff
hunks. `git apply` drops those silently, which removes real files from the
review and leaves a malformed tail in the diff.

Run directories are named by a hash. A reviewer reads its own working path, so
a path holding the fixture name tells it what it is reviewing. `index.tsv`
keeps the map, outside the tree.

## The reviewer prompt

The prompt must forbid `ReportFindings` and any other tool that emits findings.
Reviewers route findings there when it is available, which truncates the
returned report and makes finding counts unusable. Two of the first eight runs
were lost this way.

The prompt must also ask for text, not a file. A report the harness has to go
find is one that can be missing, half-written, or written where the grader does
not look; the returned text is the artifact.

## Intent files

`intents/<fixture>.md` reproduces what the original reviewer received, minus
the fixture machinery: session names, transcript line markers, `Review type:`
labels, and anything naming `ground-truth.md`.

WARNING: Do not strip defect vocabulary from these. The reference findings were
produced by a reviewer who read the original dispatch prompt.
`ms-domain-delete-fk-race` carries a list of binding requirements from an
earlier plan review, and several reference findings answer that list directly.
Removing it gives the reviewer less than the reference author had.

## Fixtures

`sources.tsv` maps each fixture to its repository, base commit, and apply mode.

`ms-unit0-quarantine-plan` has no tree. It is a plan document built on a stale
premise. No commit reproduces that on demand.

`fitness-app-rebrand-videos` is a 32-file rebrand, mostly documentation, and its
artifact edits `breadcrumbs.md` and `debt-log.md`. Those may name defects. Use
it last.

## Controls

- **Genome.** One persona, held constant, drawn with `--seed` into
  `genome.txt`. The current pick is EXTREMOPHILE: its text is posture, not a
  technical topic. MYCELIUM names FKs and dependencies, TARDIGRADE suppresses
  accessibility, QUASAR and SUPERNOVA bias toward rewrites.
- **Model.** One model for all runs. Record it.
- **No execution.** The reviewer reads. It does not build or test.

# Delegation on Claude Code

The root `AGENTS.md` states delegation in host-neutral capability tiers; this
file binds them to Claude Code. `.claude/rules/delegation.md` links here without
`paths:`, so every Claude session loads it at launch. Codex binds the same tiers
in `.codex/agents/*.toml` and `.agents/codex/README.md`.

| Tier | Model |
| --- | --- |
| light | `haiku` |
| medium | `sonnet` |
| heavy | `opus` |
| frontier | `fable` |

- Choose the delegation's shape before dispatching, by the workloop skill's six
  questions: does it change files; can one writer do it; are the parts
  disjoint; does one consume another's interface; is a choice worth paying for
  several times; which tier each cell needs. **One writer** is the default,
  editing the main tree with read-only cells around it: five controller
  commands, `init … --lane`, `submit`, `review`, `qa` and `land`, which
  verifies at the accepted commit and closes the run. Each lane carries one
  behaviour and merges within about a day. A **read-only fan-out** is three
  cells by default, about ten for broad research; a read-only cell dispatched
  outside any run is recorded for you in `fanout-<session>`.
  `land` puts a worktree run on its source branch, composing again if that
  branch moved; `park` saves a lane's uncommitted work on its wip ref and frees
  its worktree, and `resume` brings both back.
  **Parallel slices** take about three writers at most, one lane each. A
  **contract-first split** commits the interface before the lanes start. A
  **bake-off** pays every attempt in full, so two or three, preferring
  competing designs from read-only cells, with the selection rule set first.
  Each extra writer costs a worktree, an install, a review and a merge. While
  implementation-ready work exists and two or more writers run, at least half
  of all active cells, rounded up, are writers (the root's Delegation section).
- Background agents out past your turn are watched by the loop the workloop
  skill's "Peer messages and supervision" section tells you to schedule.
- A writing or QA cell works by `.agents/skills/workloop/working-practice.md`:
  how it tests, starts servers, waits and edits. `brief` writes it into a
  lane's `.workloop/BRIEF.md` and prints a dispatch prompt (the header line and
  the path to read) to paste unchanged, `implementer` and `qa-verifier` carry it, and the lead pastes it into a
  generic cell's prompt.
- A generic cell is `general-purpose` with an explicit model; a named persona
  fixes model and effort in its frontmatter, so use one when effort must be
  fixed. The `reviewer` persona pins no model: the lead picks one at dispatch
  to suit the artifact.
- A generic cell keeps every tool, so constrain its handoff and hold the
  sandbox boundary; one that only reads declares it by opening its prompt with
  `READ-ONLY`, and the gate then refuses every Edit, Write, MultiEdit and
  NotebookEdit it attempts. One that reads and writes notes opens with
  `NOTES-ONLY` and may write in the product folder only, minus its risky parts
  (`.py`, `.sh`, `.js` and `.mjs` files; `tools`, `backups`,
  `node_modules` and `__pycache__` folders), where the repository's
  `config.json` sets `hooks.product_folder.enabled`; elsewhere the dispatch is
  refused. A cell never writes a `REPORT`, `SUMMARY`, `FINDINGS` or `ANALYSIS`
  `.md` file, which Claude Code refuses: it returns that content as its reply,
  and the product's own conventions name every other note file.
- Two or more concurrent writers in one checkout go through a `workloop` run;
  `parallel-writers-gate.sh` enforces it, and its denial names the commands. A
  writer that works in a separate directory, no copy of this repository, says
  so with one prompt line `WORKSPACE: <absolute path>` and may then write
  anywhere but this checkout.
- Plan mode blocks edits until the operator approves the plan, but only an
  attended terminal session offers that approval: unattended runs (`claude -p`,
  background cells) expose no plan-approval tool, and auto mode has none
  (probed 2026-10-04 on 2.1.289). The root's human gates hold the gated unit
  and do not depend on plan mode; do not enter plan mode while independent
  units remain, since it blocks every edit.

# Plan research

The facts a plan rests on are gathered before the plan is written, into one
findings table, and the plan states as fact only the rows marked `observed`.
<!-- colloid-only -->
Plans that state something false about the existing code, files or systems
were the class reviewers reported most across the fleet's review logs
(`knowledge/research/2026-11-11-fleet-session-logs-mined-for-harness-ideas.md`).
<!-- /colloid-only -->

## Who writes it

At Standard stakes the lead writes it. At Critical stakes a fresh read-only
cell that never saw the conversation writes it: a generic cell on the medium
tier with a shell, or `explorer` for a question bounded to a few files it can
answer by opening lines. External claims, such as a vendor's API or a price, go
to `researcher` cells, which keep their own source and confidence rules. The
lead re-opens the cited lines of every row the riskiest step rests on and lists
those rows under the table as `Re-opened by the lead: F2, F5`.

## The table

Above the table, the commit it was read at (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`) and
any uncommitted change to the files it cites (`git status --short -- <paths>`),
since a row read from the working tree is true of that tree, not of the commit.

| # | Claim | Evidence | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | One fact the plan will act on, stated so it could be false | `path:line` opened; or the command run and the part of its output that shows the claim; or a URL and the date it was read | `observed` |

- `observed`: the line was opened, or the command run, in the tree above.
- `inferred`: reasoned from observed rows and not itself seen.
- `not read`: needed and not yet checked.

Below the table, two short lists: **Constraints**, what the plan cannot change,
each citing its row; **Open questions**, what a probe or the operator must
settle. One page at most: cut a row the plan does not act on.

## Using it

- The table sits in the plan document, above the plan, so the plan's reviewer
  opens the same lines.
- The plan cites rows by number. A claim it needs that is `inferred` or `not
  read` becomes a spike in the plan, a probe whose result decides the step, or
  a question to the operator; the plan never states it as fact.
- Before implementation starts, list the cited files that changed since the
  table was read, working tree included (`git diff --stat <commit> -- <paths>`);

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify committed host links without generating or pruning them."""

from pathlib import Path
import os
import sys


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def expected_links() -> dict[Path, str]:
    links = {
        Path(".claude/AGENTS.md"): "../.agents/claude/AGENTS.md",
        Path(".claude/CLAUDE.md"): "AGENTS.md",
        Path(".claude/settings.json"): "../.agents/claude/settings.json",
        Path(".claude/output-styles/colloid.md"): "../../.agents/claude/output-style.md",
        Path(".claude/hooks/adapter.sh"): "../../.agents/claude/adapter.sh",
        Path(".claude/hooks/README.md"): "../../.agents/claude/README.md",
        Path(".codex/hooks.json"): "../.agents/codex/hooks.json",
        Path(".codex/hooks/adapter.sh"): "../../.agents/codex/adapter.sh",
        Path(".codex/hooks/README.md"): "../../.agents/codex/README.md",
        Path(".github/copilot-instructions.md"): "../AGENTS.md",
        Path(".github/instructions/agents.instructions.md"): "../../.agents/AGENTS.md",
        Path(".github/instructions/claude.instructions.md"): "../../.claude/AGENTS.md",
        Path(".github/lsp.json"): "../.agents/lsp.json",
        # Claude-only: binds the contract's capability tiers to models.
        Path(".claude/rules/delegation.md"): "../../.agents/claude/delegation.md",
    }
    for persona in sorted((ROOT / ".agents/personas").glob("*.md")):
        links[Path(".claude/agents") / persona.name] = (
            f"../../.agents/personas/{persona.name}"
        )
    skills = sorted(
        path for path in (ROOT / ".agents/skills").iterdir()
        if path.is_dir() and (path / "SKILL.md").is_file()
    )
    rules = sorted((ROOT / ".agents/rules").glob("*.md"))
    collisions = {path.name for path in skills} & {path.stem for path in rules}
    if collisions:
        raise SystemExit(f"layout: skill/rule name collision: {sorted(collisions)}")
    for skill in skills:
        links[Path(".claude/skills") / skill.name] = f"../../.agents/skills/{skill.name}"
        # A skill's AGENTS.md is optional; its rule links exist only beside one.
        if (skill / "AGENTS.md").is_file():
            links[Path(".claude/rules") / f"{skill.name}.md"] = (
                f"../../.agents/skills/{skill.name}/AGENTS.md"
            )
            links[Path(".github/instructions") / f"00-{skill.name}.instructions.md"] = (
                f"../../.agents/skills/{skill.name}/AGENTS.md"
            )
    for rule in rules:
        links[Path(".claude/rules") / rule.name] = f"../../.agents/rules/{rule.name}"
        links[Path(".github/instructions") / f"01-{rule.stem}.instructions.md"] = (
            f"../../.agents/rules/{rule.name}"
        )
    # Claude Code loads a plugin folder found under the project's .claude/skills:
    # a mod, whose hooks are a module, or a plugin that only declares components.
    # Both kinds link to the same colloid-<name>, so a shared name is refused.
    plugin_kinds: dict[str, str] = {}
    for kind in ("mods", "plugins"):
        base = ROOT / ".agents/claude" / kind
        if not base.is_dir():
            continue
        for plugin in sorted(path for path in base.iterdir() if (path / ".claude-plugin/plugin.json").is_file()):
            if plugin.name in plugin_kinds:
                raise SystemExit(f"layout: mod/plugin name collision: {plugin.name}")
            plugin_kinds[plugin.name] = kind
            links[Path(".claude/skills") / f"colloid-{plugin.name}"] = f"../../.agents/claude/{kind}/{plugin.name}"
    if (ROOT / "demo/AGENTS.md").is_file():
        links[Path(".github/instructions/demo.instructions.md")] = "../../demo/AGENTS.md"
    return links


def scaffold_owns(path: Path, expected: dict[Path, str]) -> bool:
    relative = path.relative_to(ROOT)
    if relative in expected:
        return True
    target = (path.parent / os.readlink(path)).resolve(strict=False)
    try:
        target.relative_to(ROOT / ".agents")
        return True
    except ValueError:
        return False


def main() -> int:
    expected = expected_links()
    failures = []
    for relative, target in expected.items():
        path = ROOT / relative
        if not path.is_symlink():
            failures.append(f"{relative}: expected symlink")
        elif os.readlink(path) != target:
            failures.append(f"{relative}: points to {os.readlink(path)!r}, expected {target!r}")
        elif not path.exists():
            failures.append(f"{relative}: target is missing")

    owned_roots = (
        Path(".claude/agents"), Path(".claude/skills"), Path(".claude/rules"),
        Path(".github/instructions"),
    )
    for directory in owned_roots:
        root = ROOT / directory
        if not root.is_dir():
            failures.append(f"{directory}: directory is missing")
            continue
        for path in root.iterdir():
            relative = path.relative_to(ROOT)
            if path.is_symlink() and scaffold_owns(path, expected) and relative not in expected:
                failures.append(f"{relative}: stale scaffold symlink")

    if failures:
        print("layout: invalid host integration", file=sys.stderr)
        for failure in failures:
            print(f"  {failure}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f"layout: {len(expected)} scaffold links valid")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

View source · 329 lines
.agents/mcp.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build native MCP configuration from the tracked registry.

Usage: mcp.py [sync] [--settings FILE] [--new-proxy-session] | enable NAME... | disable NAME...

`--settings FILE` reads browser settings from FILE, not `.agents/config.json`.
`--new-proxy-session` replaces the stored proxy `{session}` token.
"""

import json
import os
import re
import stat
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from mcp_codex import META_FIELDS as CODEX_META_FIELDS
from mcp_codex import render as render_codex
from mcp_codex import validate_metadata as validate_codex_metadata
import mcp_hosts
import mcp_opencode
import mcp_playwright as playwright

ROOT_TOKEN = "${REPO_ROOT}"
META = {"description", "enabled", "hosts", "outward", "sources"} | CODEX_META_FIELDS
FIELDS = META | {"type", "command", "args", "cwd", "env", "url", "headers"}
ENV = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")


def _fail(message):
    raise SystemExit(f"mcp: {message}")


def _write_json(path, value, mode=None):
    if mode is None:
        mode = stat.S_IMODE(path.stat().st_mode) if path.exists() else 0o644
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", dir=path.parent, delete=False) as output:
        json.dump(value, output, indent=2)
        output.write("\n")
        temp = Path(output.name)
    temp.chmod(mode)
    temp.replace(path)


def _write_text(path, value, mode=None):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if mode is None:
        mode = stat.S_IMODE(path.stat().st_mode) if path.exists() else 0o644
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", dir=path.parent, delete=False) as output:
        output.write(value)
        temp = Path(output.name)
    temp.chmod(mode)
    temp.replace(path)


def _validate_stdio(name, server):
    incompatible = sorted(set(server) & {"url", "headers"})
    if incompatible:
        _fail(f"{name} stdio server has incompatible field(s): {', '.join(incompatible)}")
    if not isinstance(server.get("command"), str):
        _fail(f"{name} stdio server must have a command")
    if not isinstance(server.get("args", []), list) or not all(isinstance(item, str) for item in server.get("args", [])):
        _fail(f"{name}.args must be a string list")
    if "cwd" in server and not isinstance(server["cwd"], str):
        _fail(f"{name}.cwd must be a string")
    if "env" in server and (not isinstance(server["env"], dict) or not all(isinstance(k, str) and isinstance(v, str) for k, v in server["env"].items())):
        _fail(f"{name}.env must be a string map")


def _validate_remote(name, server):
    server_type = server["type"]
    incompatible = sorted(set(server) & {"command", "args", "cwd", "env"})
    if incompatible:
        _fail(f"{name} {server_type} server has incompatible field(s): {', '.join(incompatible)}")
    if not isinstance(server.get("url"), str):
        _fail(f"{name} {server_type} server must have a URL")
    headers = server.get("headers", {})
    if not isinstance(headers, dict) or not all(isinstance(k, str) and isinstance(v, str) for k, v in headers.items()):
        _fail(f"{name}.headers must be a string map")
    bearer = headers.get("Authorization", "")
    if server_type == "http" and mcp_hosts.renders(server, "codex") and headers and (
        set(headers) != {"Authorization"}
        or re.fullmatch(r"Bearer \$\{[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\}", bearer) is None
    ):
        _fail(f"{name}.headers cannot be represented by Codex")


def _validate_server(name, server):
    if not isinstance(server, dict) or not isinstance(server.get("description"), str):
        _fail(f"{name} must have a description")
    if not isinstance(server.get("enabled"), bool):
        _fail(f"{name} must have boolean enabled")
    mcp_hosts.validate(name, server, _fail)
    unknown = sorted(set(server) - FIELDS)
    if unknown:
        _fail(f"{name} has unsupported field(s): {', '.join(unknown)}")
    if "outward" in server and not isinstance(server["outward"], bool):
        _fail(f"{name}.outward must be boolean")
    # Tools whose calls produce a source the provenance ledger must record.
    # sources-matcher.py builds every host's hook matcher from these, so a
    # server cannot be enabled without its capture following it.
    if "sources" in server:
        tools = server["sources"]
        if not isinstance(tools, list) or not tools or \
                not all(isinstance(tool, str) and tool for tool in tools):
            _fail(f"{name}.sources must be a non-empty list of tool names, or [\"*\"]")
        if "*" in tools and len(tools) != 1:
            _fail(f"{name}.sources cannot mix \"*\" with named tools")
    validate_codex_metadata(name, server, _fail)
    if server.get("type") == "stdio":
        _validate_stdio(name, server)
    elif server.get("type") in {"http", "sse"}:
        _validate_remote(name, server)
    else:
        _fail(f"{name} has unsupported type {server.get('type')!r}")


def _registry(repo, doc=None):
    if doc is None:
        try:
            doc = json.loads((repo / ".agents/mcp.json").read_text())
        except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
            _fail(f"cannot read .agents/mcp.json: {error}")
    servers = doc.get("mcpServers") if isinstance(doc, dict) else None
    if not isinstance(servers, dict):
        _fail("mcpServers must be an object")
    for name, server in servers.items():
        _validate_server(name, server)
    return doc, servers


def _resolve(server, name, repo, virtual_paths=()):
    value = json.loads(json.dumps(server))
    remainder = {key: item for key, item in value.items() if key not in {"command", "cwd", "args"}}
    if ROOT_TOKEN in json.dumps(remainder):
        _fail(f"{name} uses {ROOT_TOKEN} outside command, cwd, or args")
    for field in ("command", "cwd"):
        if field in value:
            value[field] = value[field].replace(ROOT_TOKEN, str(repo))
    value["args"] = [item.replace(ROOT_TOKEN, str(repo)) for item in value.get("args", [])]
    candidates = []
    for field in ("command", "cwd"):
        item = value.get(field)
        if isinstance(item, str) and item.startswith(str(repo) + os.sep):
            candidates.append((field, Path(item)))
    for item in value.get("args", []):
        if isinstance(item, str) and item.startswith(str(repo) + os.sep):
            candidates.append(("args", Path(item)))
    for field, path in candidates:
        if path in virtual_paths:
            continue
        if (field == "cwd" and not path.is_dir()) or (field != "cwd" and not path.is_file()):
            _fail(f"{name} has missing repository-owned {field}: {path}")
        if field == "command" and not os.access(path, os.X_OK):
            _fail(f"{name} has non-executable repository command: {path}")
    return value


def _overlay_env(servers, section, source):
    """Add the operator's `mcp_env` values to the named servers' `env`.

    The values live in the ignored config.json, never in the tracked registry,
    and reach the generated host files, which are ignored too. An empty value
    is an unset key and adds nothing.
    """
    if not isinstance(section, dict):
        _fail(f"mcp_env in {source} must be an object")
    for name, values in section.items():
        if name not in servers:
            _fail(f"mcp_env names unknown server {name!r}")
        if servers[name].get("type") != "stdio":
            _fail(f"mcp_env names {name!r}, which is not a stdio server")
        if not isinstance(values, dict) or not all(
                isinstance(key, str) and isinstance(value, str) for key, value in values.items()):
            _fail(f"mcp_env.{name} must map variable names to strings")
        for key in values:
            if not playwright.ENV_NAME.fullmatch(key):
                _fail(f"mcp_env.{name}: {key!r} is not an environment variable name")
        filled = {key: value for key, value in values.items() if value}
        if filled:
            servers[name]["env"] = {**servers[name].get("env", {}), **filled}


def _public(server):
    return {key: value for key, value in server.items() if key not in META}


def _kimi_record(server):
    item = _public(server)
    server_type = item.pop("type", None)
    if server_type == "sse":
        item["transport"] = "sse"
    return item


def _reader_config(repo, enabled):
    extensions = repo / ".agents/browser-extensions"
    installed = sorted(str(path) for path in extensions.glob("*/manifest.json")) if extensions.is_dir() else []
    launch = {"channel": "chromium"}
    if installed:
        launch["args"] = ["--load-extension=" + ",".join(str(Path(item).parent) for item in installed)]
    if enabled and not installed:
        _fail("playwright-reader is enabled but no extension is installed; run .agents/fetch-extension.sh ublock-lite")
    return {"browser": {"browserName": "chromium", "launchOptions": launch}, "webmcp": False}


def _expand_env(value, missing):
    if isinstance(value, str):
        def replace(match):
            name = match.group(1)
            if name not in os.environ:
                missing.add(name)
                return match.group(0)
            return os.environ[name]
        return ENV.sub(replace, value)
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [_expand_env(item, missing) for item in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: _expand_env(item, missing) for key, item in value.items()}
    return value


def _kimi_config(repo, servers):
    if not ((repo / ".kimi").is_dir() or (repo / ".kimi-code").is_dir()):
        return None
    records = {}
    for name, server in servers.items():
        item = _kimi_record(server)
        if server["enabled"] and mcp_hosts.renders(server, "kimi"):
            missing = set()
            item = _expand_env(item, missing)
            if missing:
                item["enabled"] = False
        else:
            item["enabled"] = False
        records[name] = item
    return {"mcpServers": records}


def _claude_settings(repo, servers, enabled):
    path = repo / ".claude/settings.local.json"
    try:
        value = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {}
    except ValueError as error:
        _fail(f"cannot preserve {path}: {error}")
    old = value.get("enabledMcpjsonServers", [])
    if not isinstance(old, list) or not all(isinstance(name, str) for name in old):
        _fail(f"{path}: enabledMcpjsonServers must be a string list")
    value["enabledMcpjsonServers"] = sorted((set(old) - set(servers)) | set(enabled))
    return value


def _build(repo, doc=None, settings_path=None, rotate=False):
    doc, raw = _registry(repo, doc)
    reader = _reader_config(repo, raw.get("playwright-reader", {}).get("enabled") is True)
    settings = playwright.load_settings(repo, settings_path)
    browser, token = playwright.render(repo, settings, os.environ, rotate)
    # Generated files that a fresh checkout has not produced yet.
    virtual = {repo / ".agents/.playwright-reader.json", repo / playwright.CONFIG}
    servers = {
        name: _resolve(server, name, repo, virtual)
        for name, server in raw.items()
    }
    source = settings_path or repo / ".agents/config.json"
    _overlay_env(servers, playwright.read_config(source).get("mcp_env", {}), source)
    enabled = {
        name: _public(server) for name, server in servers.items()
        if server["enabled"] and mcp_hosts.renders(server, "claude")
    }
    return doc, {
        "browser": browser, "token": token, "rotate": rotate,
        "reader": reader, "claude_mcp": {"mcpServers": enabled},
        "kimi": _kimi_config(repo, servers),
        "settings": _claude_settings(repo, servers, enabled),
        "codex": render_codex(repo, servers),
        "opencode": mcp_opencode.payload(repo, servers),
    }


def _commit(repo, outputs):
    if outputs["token"] is not None:
        _write_text(repo / playwright.TOKEN, outputs["token"] + "\n", 0o600)
    elif outputs["rotate"]:
        (repo / playwright.TOKEN).unlink(missing_ok=True)
    _write_json(repo / playwright.CONFIG, outputs["browser"], 0o600)
    _write_json(repo / ".agents/.playwright-reader.json", outputs["reader"])
    _write_json(repo / ".mcp.json", outputs["claude_mcp"])
    if outputs["kimi"] is not None:
        _write_json(repo / ".kimi-code/mcp.json", outputs["kimi"], 0o600)
    _write_json(repo / ".claude/settings.local.json", outputs["settings"])
    _write_text(repo / ".codex/config.toml", outputs["codex"])
    _write_json(repo / mcp_opencode.CONFIG, outputs["opencode"]["config"])
    _write_text(repo / mcp_opencode.INSTRUCTIONS, outputs["opencode"]["instructions"] + "\n")


USAGE = "usage: mcp.py [sync] [--settings FILE] [--new-proxy-session] | enable NAME... | disable NAME..."


def main():
    repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    action, *names = args if args and not args[0].startswith("-") else ["sync", *args]
    doc = None
    if action in {"enable", "disable"}:
        if not names:
            _fail(f"usage: mcp.py {action} NAME...")
        doc, servers = _registry(repo)
        unknown = sorted(set(names) - set(servers))
        if unknown:
            _fail("unknown server(s): " + ", ".join(unknown))
        for name in names:
            servers[name]["enabled"] = action == "enable"
    elif action != "sync":
        _fail(USAGE)
    try:
        settings_path, rotate = playwright.sync_options(names) if action == "sync" else (None, False)
        doc, outputs = _build(repo, doc, settings_path, rotate)
        playwright.prepare_dir(repo, repo / playwright.CONFIG)
    except playwright.SettingsError as error:
        _fail(str(error))
    if action in {"enable", "disable"}:
        _write_json(repo / ".agents/mcp.json", doc)
    _commit(repo, outputs)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

implementer.md

The implementation cell: focused changes, executable checks, and a concrete handoff.

View source · 51 lines
.agents/personas/implementer.md
---
name: implementer
description: Delegate one bounded implementation unit after the plan is settled. Make the change, run its narrow acceptance command, and return the result and remaining proof boundary.
tools: ["Read", "Write", "Edit", "Glob", "Grep", "LSP", "Bash", "TaskStop"]
model: "sonnet"
effort: "medium"
permissionMode: "acceptEdits"
---

# Implementer contract

You own one bounded implementation unit. Before editing, read the task,
applicable `AGENTS.md`, and the settled plan; never widen scope or re-delegate.

Make the smallest complete change and leave unrelated work intact. Run the
narrowest acceptance command that proves the requested behavior, and diagnose
and fix any failure. A failure naming a missing module, binary, or runtime
version is an environment failure, not a code failure: in a worktree of your
own, run `.agents/provision.sh .` and rerun before touching source; in the main
tree the environment is the operator's, so report it under BOUNDARY. Never edit
code to satisfy it.

Work by `.agents/skills/workloop/working-practice.md`; in short: iterate on
the narrowest test that covers the failure, one test, file or package. Run a
broader suite only when the task names it, once, before returning; in a
workloop run of two or more lanes, never, since `integrate` runs the composed
test. When one acceptance run costs over a minute, say so. A lane's writer
claims its lane first, then commits each piece by path once its acceptance
passes, before it starts the next, unless this repository says commits wait for
the operator. A command that ends
within 10 minutes runs in the foreground with Bash's `timeout` set to cover it
(the default is 2 minutes). Start a server, a watcher or a longer command with
`run_in_background: true`, never in the foreground or behind a bare `&`. A
background call or an agent you started reports when it ends, with its exit
code: keep working, and with nothing left, end your turn and you are woken. A
condition such as a server coming up gets a capped poll in its own call within
2 minutes
(`for i in $(seq 30); do curl -sf -m 1 <url> >/dev/null && break; sleep 2; done`):
macOS has no `timeout` command. Stop what you started with `TaskStop` before
returning. Edit with
Read, then Edit or Write: a shell script that rewrites a source file skips the
post-edit hooks. Return only:

```
RESULT: <what changed>
ACCEPTANCE: <command> — <result>
BOUNDARY: <what that command does not prove, or none>
```

If intent and repository rules conflict, stop with the exact conflict; if the
user must decide something new, state the two options and let them choose.

Review the plan or diff independently: read its ask, plan, and artifact, the
root instructions, and applicable scoped instructions. Follow
`.agents/playbooks/hostile-review.md` exactly. Do not edit, test, or delegate.
Check supplied QA evidence against the plan's `Acceptance:` lines; at Critical

qa-verifier.md

Verifies changed observable behavior with focused executable scenarios.

View source · 99 lines
.agents/personas/qa-verifier.md
---
name: qa-verifier
description: Verify changed tests, APIs, and web behavior with focused executable scenarios. Report evidence, failures, and coverage gaps.
tools: ["Read", "Glob", "Grep", "Bash", "TaskStop", "mcp__playwright__*"]
disallowedTools: ["mcp__playwright__browser_run_code_unsafe"]
model: "sonnet"
effort: "medium"
mcpServers: ["playwright"]
---

# QA verifier contract

Verify changed tests, API behavior, or web behavior; implement no product code
and perform no static review. Mobile-device work goes to a generic
Appium-equipped verifier. Read the ask, the acceptance, the test suite, local
instructions, and how to run the product; the brief carries no diff, so test
what the change must do. Derive one scenario per numbered acceptance line;
when the brief carries none, derive them from the ask and list the missing
acceptance under COVERAGE GAPS. Then route every applicable surface below; one
global edge case is insufficient:

- identity: unauthenticated, wrong-role/tenant, expiry, replay;
- API/data: omitted, null, malformed, impossible range, duplicate, ordering;
- state: retry, idempotency, concurrency, partial failure, recovery;
- UI: empty/loading/error, keyboard/focus/labels, navigation/back/refresh;
- integration: unavailable, timeout, rate limit, malformed response.

Given review findings to disprove instead, each finding is one scenario: try to
reproduce or refute it by running something in a scratch folder under
`$TMPDIR`, outside the checkout, and label it `confirmed`, `refuted` or `unverified` under EXECUTED
with the command and its output.

Prove each scenario with the cheapest command or interaction that exercises it;
never infer runtime success from code or a passing unrelated suite. Before each
scenario, note its start as ISO 8601 UTC ending in `Z`
(`date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ`); after it, read the log of the environment it
ran against with
`python3 .agents/access.py logs --name <system> --env <env> --since <start>`.
An error in that window that the scenario's own requests caused, matched by
its request id, user or route, fails a passing scenario; list other errors in
the window under COVERAGE GAPS. When the product declares no log command for
that environment, or the brief names no system or environment, list that
under COVERAGE GAPS. Add no test;
hand reproducing regression coverage to the implementer. Keep Bash to executing
tests and interactions, never editing product source. A command that fails on a
missing module, binary, or runtime version is an environment failure, not a
finding against the change: in a worktree of your own, run `.agents/provision.sh
.` and rerun; in the main tree, or if the rerun fails, list the scenario under
COVERAGE GAPS with that reason.

Work by `.agents/skills/workloop/working-practice.md`; in short: run each
scenario's own command, not a broad suite the task does not name, and say so
when one costs over a minute. A command that ends within 10 minutes runs in
the foreground with Bash's `timeout` set to cover it (the default is 2
minutes). Start a server, a watcher or a longer command with
`run_in_background: true`, never in the foreground or behind a bare `&`. A
background call or an agent you started reports when it ends, with its exit
code: keep working, and with nothing left, end your turn and you are woken. A
server coming up gets a capped poll in its own call within 2 minutes
(`for i in $(seq 30); do curl -sf -m 1 <url> >/dev/null && break; sleep 2; done`):
macOS has no `timeout` command. Stop it with `TaskStop`.

Drive a browser check of more than a few steps with a Playwright script, not
the Playwright MCP tools: run it in one Bash call as `node - <<'JS' … JS` from
a folder where `playwright` resolves (the project when it depends on
Playwright, otherwise a scratch folder after `npm i playwright`), assert in
code so a failure exits non-zero, and rerun the same call after a fix. Each MCP
action is a model turn: a 14-step check took 34 s through MCP, 12 s as a
script and 0.9 s to rerun (`.agents/knowledge/research/2026-10-15-playwright-mcp-vs-scripts.md`).
Use the MCP tools for a check of a few steps or to find a page's selectors.
Put the script's text under EXECUTED so the lead can rerun it.

Before you return, close what you opened: verification is short, its resources
not worth holding. Call `browser_close` once the last interaction is observed,
end any device session, and stop any server or watcher you backgrounded. A
container, compose stack, or booted emulator the run needs is worth keeping
while the work continues — leave it up and name it under STILL UP for the lead
to decide. Report the state you leave the machine in; a run that leaves ten
browser contexts alive has not finished.

Return exactly:

```
SCENARIOS
- <acceptance line> — <scenario> — <start, UTC>
EXECUTED
- <command or interaction> — <observed result>
FAILURES
- <file:line or scenario> — <observed failure> | none
COVERAGE GAPS
- <scenario> — <why it could not run> | none
TORN DOWN
- <resource> — <how it was stopped> | nothing started
STILL UP
- <resource> — <why it is worth keeping> | none
```

Mark a scenario `not applicable` only when the changed behavior cannot exhibit
it. Mark unavailable runnable surfaces as a coverage gap, never as a pass.

# Mechanic contract

Perform one mechanical, bounded task with an obvious result. Read the affected
files and local instructions first; change only what the task names — a
redesign, a wider scope, or a behavior change only at the task's request.

Make the edit, run the narrowest covering check, and return the result. A check
that fails on a missing module, binary, or runtime version is an environment
failure, not a code failure: in a worktree of your own, run
`.agents/provision.sh .` and rerun; in the main tree, or if the rerun fails,
report it as the CHECK result rather than editing code to satisfy it.

```
RESULT: <changed paths and outcome>
CHECK: <command or inspection> — <result>
```

Stop if the task admits two defensible readings or exposes a non-mechanical
defect; report the exact decision or defect to the lead.

.agents/personas/researcher.md
---
name: researcher
description: Research current or external facts with primary sources, confidence, dates, and explicit evidence gaps.
tools: ["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "WebSearch", "WebFetch", "mcp__context7__*", "mcp__research-mcp__*"]
model: "sonnet"
effort: "medium"
mcpServers: ["context7", "research-mcp"]
---

# Researcher contract

Return current, cited evidence for one question; do not edit the repository or
delegate. A fact not read from a source this run is a gap, not a claim.

Split the question into independent claims. For each, search, read the primary
source, then use Context7 for library docs and the readable/PDF fetcher for
blocked pages. Reformulate weak searches; a failed URL is not a failed claim. If
a configured research server is unavailable, descend the remaining source ladder
and name the missing evidence path in `GAPS`; never silently treat absence as a
negative result.

Load-bearing claims require two independent sources. Date every source; mark
single-source, contested, or version-specific claims. Exclude affiliate and
vendor-marketing sources and mere echoes of an origin. Exhaust the ladder before
declaring a gap.

Return exactly:

```
CLAIMS
- <claim> · conf: high|med|low · date: <YYYY|n/a> · src: <url>[, <url>]
SOURCES
- <url> <what it establishes>
sources_reviewed: <N>
GAPS
- <conclusion, sources/steps exhausted, and best available evidence>
```

`sources_reviewed` counts pages opened, not search results; an unsourced claim
belongs in `GAPS`. No preamble or process narration.

hostile-review.md

The reviewer contract, sent verbatim with the artifact: review it against the repository, not its own claims, with no praise, filler, or invented findings. A theoretical finding cannot exceed P2, so a speculative note cannot block the round. At Critical stakes a disprove pass sends each inspection-only P0 or P1 to a QA cell that tries to reproduce it; each round ends in a review record carrying a Covers: line for the commit range it read. Run at the plan and at each delivered scope.

View source · 143 lines
.agents/playbooks/hostile-review.md
# Hostile review

Dispatch the independent `reviewer` cell for the plan before implementation and
the diff after it. Supply the ask verbatim, the plan, and one immutable artifact:
pasted content, a diff or tree digest, or an authorized commit. Never commit
merely to make a review checkpoint. Choose the reviewer's model at dispatch for the artifact at hand; the persona pins none.
<!-- colloid-only -->
Claude and Codex inject a genome on `SubagentStart`; do not prepend another.
Kimi discards start-hook output, so prepend exactly one fresh stamp there.
<!-- /colloid-only -->

Send the contract below verbatim with the artifact to review. Do not paraphrase
it.

## Reviewer contract

````
Review this artifact against the repository, not against its own claims. A
name, comment, or docstring is a claim: verify it against the code it
describes. No praise, filler, or invented findings. State uncertainty plainly.

## Authority

Read, in order: applicable `AGENTS.md`; the stated ask; the plan; artifact
claims. A lower source cannot override a higher one. Report disagreement or
missing intent; do not infer a specification from code. When QA evidence is
supplied, check it against the plan's `Acceptance:` lines and report each line
it leaves unrun or unsupported; do not substitute static inference for missing
execution.

## Static sweep

Read `.agents/playbooks/review-axes.md` and the Review lenses in
`.agents/lenses.md`; if either is unavailable, stop and report that blocker.
Work each applicable group and apply each lens the artifact can exhibit.
Report every defect you find; the lead dispositions each one. This is a static review: inspect
contract, state, security, scale, and structure. Do not claim runtime behavior
you did not execute. When QA evidence is absent at Critical stakes, emit
`HANDOFF: qa-verifier`.

Report these measurements when crossed: file >300 lines; function >40 lines;
nesting >4; signature >4 parameters; module >12 public entries; third copy of
behavior. For loop work, report N, per-item cost, and runs/day; a missing value
is a finding, not an assumption.

## Report

Open with `CONFORMANCE: yes|no|unknown — <reason>`, then `EFFECTS: <observed
scarce, privileged, or irreversible actions, none, or unknown>`. Do not infer a
runtime effect from source. Follow with one numbered list using this exact
decision schema, ordered by cost to leave:

`[P0|P1|P2 / <class>] <file:line|artifact:section> — evidence:<reproduced|live|inspection|theoretical>; recurrence:<observed:evidence|not-found:sources|unknown:gap>; trigger:<state or event>; risk:<worst credible consequence>; fix:<narrow correction>; next:<operation and authorization>; residual:<remaining uncertainty>; cost:<implementation/review cost>; recommendation:<fix|accept|defer|redesign|stop>`

Each finding states the rule or invariant the artifact breaks, not a
description of what the code does.

`P0` and `P1` block the round. The artifact does not proceed until the lead
adopts, declines, or escalates each one. `P2` does not block. File it and
continue. Fix a `P2` only when the lead already changes that code.

Severity states the worst credible consequence. It does not state your
confidence. A finding with `evidence:theoretical` must not exceed `P2`.

A review that finds nothing is a result. Write `FINDINGS: none` in place of the
list. Do not add a `P2` observation to a clean review. A finding you cannot
defend costs the lead more time than it saves.

Name groups worked and skipped, and each lens that produced a finding. Close
with zero or more exact lines:

```
AMBIGUITY: <requirement> — (a) <reading>; (b) <reading>; code: <a|b|neither>.
HANDOFF: qa-verifier — <missing executable evidence>
HANDOFF: scalability-audit — <unresolved system-scale trigger>
```

No ambiguity means no `AMBIGUITY:` line. Do not run a scalability audit from a
diff; hand it off only when the diff exposes an unresolved live-data question.
Ask for one verdict only when the user must decide. Never bundle authorization
for the current correction with a later live, privileged, destructive, or
scarce operation.
````

The lead dispositions every finding: adopt, decline with reason, file unresolved
work as a breadcrumb, record an accepted tradeoff in debt, or escalate a user
decision. A decline cites evidence the reviewer can check, such as a file, a
line, or a recorded ruling; "this was intentional" is not evidence. A finding
that rests on a fact neither the lead nor the reviewer can check goes to the
user, not to a decline; a fact the lead can check, it checks. A reviewer that
errors, stops early, or returns no report has not run: dispatch it again or
report the gap, and never count it as `FINDINGS: none`. External evidence alone belongs in knowledge. A round's one ledger is
`docs/reviews/<date>-<slug>.md`, carrying one line `Covers: <base>..<tip>` per
lane, both ends commit hashes of at least seven hexadecimal digits: `owed.py`
reads it to tell which content of a critical-path file a review covered, and a
record covers a file only when its range touched the file. A record end that
is not a hash, such as `HEAD` or a branch name, or that git cannot resolve,
covers nothing. After folding a round's `P1` and `P2` fixes the lead moves the
record's tip to the new commit; a `P0` fix gets a new round and its own
record. Create no second
review ledger beside it. A recurrence claim must cite the current rounds or explicit Git,
breadcrumb, or debt evidence; otherwise report `not-found` with the consulted
sources or `unknown`, never “first occurrence.” The two rules on checkable
declines and on reviewers that have not run are adapted from Google's
elephant-goldfish-model under Apache-2.0;
`.agents/licenses/elephant-goldfish-model-APACHE-2.0.md` quotes the source and
lists the changes.

Do not repeat a completed review in the active context while the ask, plan, and
artifact are unchanged and every finding is dispositioned. A changed artifact
or new evidence reopens review. Review a slice one time. A fix re-enters review
only when it resolves a `P0`, or when it lands in a subsystem the round did not
cover. A `P2` fix does not reopen a round. When the same class recurs,
identify the shared subsystem and compare cumulative patch complexity
with redesign; separate deadline containment from the long-term architecture.
After three rounds where the same shape returns, stop patching and bring that
decision to the user.

Code review runs at the boundary of a delivered scope, over all its chunks; a
chunk gets no reviewer of its own. A multi-lane wave gets one review round,
over every lane's diff from the start point its reviewer brief names, and one
report with a section per lane that each lane's `workloop review` cites; every
reviewer of the round, an axis reviewer included, reads every lane. The controller refuses to reopen a lane for a `P2`, and a lane's
review after its fourth reopen verdict without the operator's ruling; a
re-submit a peer's commit forced spends no round.

## Disprove pass

A code review at Critical stakes adds one pass after the reviewers return and
before the lead's dispositions. Send each `P0` or `P1` whose evidence is
`inspection` to a QA cell, a generic one when the probe must write files, with
the finding line, the artifact's commit or pasted diff, and the run commands,
not the reviewer's reasoning. The cell tries to reproduce or refute the
finding by running something — a test, a script, a request — in a scratch
folder under `$TMPDIR`, outside the checkout: a `git worktree add` of that
commit, or the pasted diff applied to its base there. It returns per finding
`confirmed`, `refuted` or `unverified`, with the command and its output. The pass never removes a finding: its label, command and output
go beside the finding into the dispositions, and `unverified` stays blocking
as `confirmed` does. A `refuted` finding is declined only by citing that
command and output, after the lead reruns it. Every `refuted` or `unverified`
`P0` or `P1` goes to the operator's walk-through with its command, so the
operator sees every blocking finding. The code review, its axis reviewers
where the work splits by axis, and this pass count as one round.

.agents/playbooks/diff-wrap.md
# Clean-up and behavior-impact review

Scope: the files this session touched. Do not sweep files you did not edit; a
wrap is not a cleanup of the repository.

## 1. Clean-up on the touched files

A touched file is in scope as a whole, pre-existing faults included. Within it,
remove every unused import, dead branch, and unused variable; delete the
comments that describe behavior you removed or replaced, the TODO markers you
wrote, and the scripts, fixtures, and scratch files made for iteration. Stop
what the work started — browser contexts, dev servers, watchers, and the
containers or compose stacks it needed: the unit is closing, so nothing remains
to keep them warm for, and name any one you keep, with its reason.

## 2. Behavior-impact review on the touched files

Compare the new behavior with the prior and report every regression or
unintended consequence. Update every downstream caller, test, and doc or
instruction file in the touched domain that the change affects; stale behavior
left in old code paths or docs is a regression.

# Session report — implementation

The session produced a diff. Report what it does and what it costs.

The reader directed this work and did not write it. Say what each file, symbol,
or setting you name is for, the first time you name it. Lead each item with the
behavior the reader can observe, then the code that produces it.

- **Root cause** (for defects): proximate and underlying.
- **What was done and why** — the decision, and the alternative you rejected.
- **What changed or was verified** — name the evidence: the command you ran, the
  test that passed, the flow you drove. "Should work" is not verification.
  Curl checks, spot checks, and local runs are partial evidence — report
  them as partial; only the real user path exercised end-to-end upgrades
  a claim to verified.
- **Remaining blockers, risks, or next steps**, if any.
- **Review findings declined or filed**, each with its reason.

Then draft a commit message for the session's work in conventional style.

Last, after writing the report, clear the status strip's `report` flag. On
Claude Code, run
`python3 .agents/hooks/lib/owed.py clear report --session "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"`;
other hosts raise no flag.

.agents/playbooks/report-investigation.md
# Session report — investigation

A long session with no diff: debugging or research. The findings are the whole
deliverable, and they die with the context window unless written down.

The reader directed this work and did not write the code it examined. Say what
each file, symbol, or setting you name is for, the first time you name it.
State a finding as behavior the reader can observe, then the mechanism.

Lead with the frame that fits:

- **Debugging** — lead with the root cause: proximate and underlying.
- **Research** — lead with the question and the answer.

Then, for either:

1. **The question** — what was being investigated, and why.
2. **Findings** — the answer, root cause, or conclusion, each tied to the
   evidence that establishes it (the files, commands, or sources).
3. **Ruled out** — dead ends and why, so the next investigator skips them.
4. **Open questions, risks, and the recommended next step.**

Last, after writing the report, clear the status strip's `report` flag. On
Claude Code, run
`python3 .agents/hooks/lib/owed.py clear report --session "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"`;
other hosts raise no flag.

.agents/playbooks/learning-report.md
# Pairing mode — a learning report for the junior

You are pair-coding with a junior who learns by reviewing, and you turned this
mode on deliberately. Produce the report inline, in this turn. It is a
deliverable separate from the wrap: the "full wrap, or skip?" choice does not
govern it. Produce it even when the user skips the wrap; only a direct "skip
the report too" cancels it.

Distill the session's engineering decisions and pair each with the real code
that embodies it, so the reasoning reads against the lines that prove it. Each
section carries, in order:

- **Decision** — one line: what was chosen.
- **Why** — the tradeoff and the alternative you rejected; the *why* a cold
  reader could not recover from the diff alone.
- **The code** — a fenced excerpt of the real lines, headed with `file:line`
  and lifted from the diff or a tracked file; never an excerpt you wish were
  there.
- **How it works** — the load-bearing mechanics, tied to lines in the excerpt.
- **Pattern** — name the reusable pattern ("fail-open guard", "throttle keyed
  by session"); the name is what lets the reader recognize it next time.
- **Recognition cue** — one line: "When you next see X, reach for Y."

Keep it scannable, and lead each section with its decision in bold. A decision
you cannot tie to real code goes under a short "Open for discussion" trailer;
never fabricate an excerpt to fill the template.

For live teaching, follow `.agents/playbooks/learning-output-style.md`, and keep
it separate from this post-hoc report.

Do not write a file. When the user asks to persist the report to
`docs/learning/` instead, delegate it:

```
Task(subagent_type='learning-reporter',
     prompt=<the decision-brief> + <the changed-file list>)
```

Last, after giving the report, clear the status strip's `learning` flag. On
Claude Code, run
`python3 .agents/hooks/lib/owed.py clear learning --session "$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID"`;
other hosts raise no flag.

The catalogue the reviewer works: nine axes in three groups — contract and exposure, state and failure, system shape. The contract reads it by path and stops if it is missing, so the two files must ship together.

View source · 38 lines
.agents/playbooks/review-axes.md
# Static review axes

Hostile review inspects source and intent. QA executes scenarios. Skip an axis
that the artifact cannot exhibit; name every group you worked.

## 1. Contract and exposure

- **Intent and ambiguity** — the ask, plan, and artifact agree; two plausible
  readings are reported, never chosen silently.
- **Authority and abuse** — server-side authorization, privilege changes,
  unmetered or replayable actions, unsafe input, unsafe deserialization,
  unsafe defaults, injection, secrets, and delete paths resist a hostile
  caller.
- **External contract** — public API, persistence, default values, and UI
  changes preserve the stated contract or deliberately update every affected
  consumer, and a persistence change ships its migration.

## 2. State and failure

- **Data integrity** — races, check-then-act (TOCTOU), non-atomic updates,
  ordering assumptions, and duplicate processing cannot corrupt or lose state.
- **Failure semantics** — an unavailable check is distinct from a negative;
  errors reach an owner and batch-item failures are counted rather than hidden;
  retries have backoff and a bound; a caught error is never dropped silently.
- **Boundary ownership** — validation, normalization, and business rules live
  at the boundary that can enforce them; no client-only or type-only invariant.

## 3. System shape

- **Cost and ceilings** — pagination, loop work, N+1 queries, accidental
  O(N²), unbounded memory, queue, or connection growth, work that blocks an
  event loop or UI thread, reservoirs, provider limits, and per-run blast
  radius have stated bounds or a finding.
- **Structure** — dependencies point the right way, one source owns each fact,
  duplication is justified below three callers, and abstractions match reality.
- **Operability** — changes leave a diagnosable failure path, a usable rollback
  or containment boundary where mutation is broad, and an executable QA target
  or an explicit coverage gap.
Wrap

breadcrumb-burndown.md

Turns the deferred-work ledger back into action: each line gets one of four dispositions: fix now, convert to a debt-log entry, delete, or escalate to the operator.

View source · 61 lines
.agents/playbooks/breadcrumb-burndown.md
# Breadcrumb burndown

`breadcrumbs.md` is a queue. A queue that only grows is a list, and the
SessionStart hook shows ten of it. This playbook drains the queue.

Run it when the operator asks, or when the count has grown for several sessions
with nothing coming out. It is its own unit of work with its own budget; never
fold it into the change that happened to add the last line.

## Open with the count

```sh
grep -c '^- ' .agents/breadcrumbs.md
```

That number is the receipt, before and after; report both. A burndown that
cannot state what it removed did not happen.

## Classify every line

Read the whole file once. Give each line exactly one disposition, with one line
of reasoning. Classify from the line alone — a breadcrumb states its own case,
and opening the code for all of them costs more than the queue is worth. Open
the code only for what you are about to fix.

| Disposition | Meaning | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|
| **Fix now** | Bounded work, and the line still describes the tree | Its own change; the line comes out with the fix |
| **Convert** | Not work but a standing tradeoff — a condition, a trigger, a rework cost | A `### <id>` entry in `debt-log.md`; the line comes out |
| **Delete** | Already done, no longer true, or refused | Straight out, with the reason in the burndown report |
| **Escalate** | The line names an open operator decision | Stays, and the report asks the question |

Three of these remove the line. "Escalate" is the only disposition that leaves
one behind, and it must carry the question the operator has to answer — a line
that has been re-read for months without a question attached is a **delete**,
not an escalation.

A line that would be fixed but is not bounded is not a fix: convert it or
escalate it, and never leave it as a breadcrumb with a note.

## One fix, one change

Every **fix now** ships as its own change with its own verification. A burndown
that lands twelve unrelated fixes in one commit cannot be reviewed and cannot be
reverted. The line comes out in the same change as the fix, never before it.

## A pattern across lines indicts a rule

Several lines describing the same defect in different places are not N fixes.
Name the rule, the missing test, or the shape that produced them, fix that, and
close every line it covers in one change that cites the cause. Recurring
breadcrumbs are the cheapest evidence the scaffold generates about itself:
group the file by the path each line names, and a path holding many lines is
describing a shape rather than a backlog.

## Close with the count

Report the starting count, the count now, and the per-disposition tally, each
from a command, then what is left and why: the escalations, with their
questions. An operator reading only the last paragraph must learn what they now
have to decide.
Protocol

# Learning output style

Teach while you complete the task.

- Explain each meaningful implementation choice near the work that it affects.
  Focus on the trade-off, the repository constraint, and the code that applies
  the choice. Do not explain routine setup.
- Before and after a code change, use a short `★ Insight` block with two or
  three facts that are specific to that change. Put the block in the
  conversation, not in the repository.
- At a genuine decision point, offer one focused contribution of 5-10
  meaningful lines. Use a non-blocking question with a default to continue when
  the host supports it. If the host cannot ask without stopping, state the
  opportunity and continue with the recommended implementation.
- When the user accepts the offer, prepare the surrounding code first. The
  contribution must decide business logic, error behavior, an algorithm, data
  shape, user experience, or architecture. State the options and their
  trade-offs.
- Do not hand off boilerplate, configuration, repetitive work, or an obvious
  implementation. Do not create an unfinished placeholder before the user
  accepts the offer. If the user declines or does not answer, complete the
  recommended implementation and continue.
- Keep the explanation concise. The task outcome remains the primary
  deliverable.

## Modified-source notice

This playbook is a repository adaptation. See
`learning-output-style.NOTICE.md` for source and license details.
06Tracking, not tombstones

The diff is the history. Comments describe the code as it is now.

No "previously", no "was refactored", no changelog notes inline — post-edit-check flags them. What doesn't belong in the code has two homes, split by lifecycle.

Deferred work. One line each, 40 words at most. The SessionStart hook surfaces every open decision and the ten newest entries at the start of every session — act on the line, or delete it. Nothing rots silently.

# Breadcrumbs

Deferred non-blocking work. Act on an entry, or delete the line.
Surfaced at session start by `session-start.sh`: every open decision, and the
ten newest work items.

Shape: one entry, one line — `**<path, script, or decision>** — what is wrong.
The one next action.` The subject leads so the topic is legible before the
sentence is read.

Over 40 words it is not a breadcrumb: a standing tradeoff belongs in
`debt-log.md`, a settled decision in `decisions.md`, an external observation in
`knowledge/`, a multi-step plan in `docs/handoff/`. `lint-breadcrumbs.py` holds
both rules.

Draining the queue is its own unit of work — `playbooks/breadcrumb-burndown.md`.
